extras.verified_at_basis: the 30 GB uncompressed per-build ceiling is stated on the butler pushing page
extras.quota_verbatim: 30 GB uncompressed per build ('the itch.io backend will reject builds with a total uncompressed size that exceeds 30GB'). No documented total-account storage cap; project pages have a soft limit of 20, raisable on request. Free to host, unlimited downloads.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: 30 GB uncompressed per build/channel; per-object-cap on HTML5 embeds: 500 MB total extracted and 200 MB per single extracted file; web uploader caps at 2 GB (500 MB default) but butler has no such limit; request-rate not a practical constraint. Retention: builds persist until deleted; no TTL.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free and unmetered — 'There is no limit to downloads' (itch.io support reply). Files served from itch.zone CDN.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 30 GB per build x unlimited channels per project (channel name is arbitrary: windows, osx, bonus, dlc-1, shard-01...) x up to 20+ projects per free account. 1 project x 20 channels = 600 GB on one free account. Each build is independently addressable and downloadable.
extras.tooling_verbatim: `butler` CLI (butler push / butler download / butler status) plus the Wharf HTTP API — GET https://api.itch.io/wharf/latest?target=user/game&channel_name=X returns the build manifest. butler does rsync-style block diffing so re-pushes are cheap.
extras.agent_focus: game platforms as storage: cloud saves, game backends, mod hosting. Per-user total caps and whether save data is retrievable via API.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
